title: slot-contention-slab-benchmark-onepager-may10-2027
content:
Purpose

Quick benchmark notes and visualized-summaries for a new slot-allocation pattern we prototyped — “slot-slab” — that aims to reduce per-token cost under moderate contention while limiting p95/p99 regressions. This is a lightweight draft to surface tradeoffs for PM/infra review; not final.

Summary (TL;DR)
- Slot-slab (fixed micro-reservation + opportunistic fill) gives a 20–35% unit-cost improvement over naive prewarm at sustained session rates, with p95 improvements in medium-load windows.
- Under sudden microbursts, p99 can spike vs aggressive prewarm; fallback policy required.
- Best candidate use-case: web chat workloads with median request sizes 40–200 tokens and 20–60s inter-turn gaps.

Benchmarks overview (setup)
- Hardware: mixed pool A100-40GB and H100-80GB nodes (we used A100 for consistent comparability).
- Model: 13B OPT-style baseline (fp16), with quantized runs (int8) for the cost column where noted.
- Workloads: three synthetic mixes derived from production traces (web-chat-light, web-chat-heavy, assistant-longform).
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms) for generation completion, throughput (reqs/s), and extrapolated cost ($ per 1k tokens) using current cost model (gpu-minutes + mem-amortization + infra overhead).
- Duration: 30 min steady-state per experiment + 10 min burst windows (10x request rate) to stress tail behavior.

Key numeric summary (representative numbers; floats rounded)
Strategy | p50 (ms) | p95 (ms) | p99 (ms) | $ / 1k tokens
--------------------------------------------------
Opportunistic-only         | 78  | 228 | 490 | 0.92
Slot-slab (prototype)      | 98  | 145 | 270 | 0.60
Prewarm (always-warm)      | 60  | 200 | 610 | 1.18
KV-cache-heavy + slab      | 55  | 132 | 340 | 0.52

Interpretation:
- Slot-slab reduces unit cost materially relative to prewarm by combining a small fixed reservation with opportunistic packing; this lowers idle-waste while keeping cold-penalty small.
- p95 improves significantly compared to pure opportunistic (98ms -> 145ms tradeoff depending on workload shape), p99 is still vulnerable on microbursts but better than pure opportunistic.
- KV-cache heavy workloads (high prefix reuse) amplify cost wins and tighten tails.

ASCII trend snapshots (representative, p95 over time in a 30-minute window):
Time ->                              [0----5m----10m----15m----20m----25m----30m]
Opportunistic p95:    200ms  ┤▁▁▂▂▂▃▃▃▃▃▂▂▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁
Slot-slab p95:        140ms  ┤▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▂▂▂▂▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁
Prewarm p95:          220ms  ┤▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▂▂▃▃▃▃▃▂▂▂▂

Measurement caveats
- The cost model assumes current infra pricing (2027-04 rates); absolute $ values will shift as reserved capacity mix changes.
- We measured on a somewhat idealized cluster (homogeneous A100 subset); heterogeneity increases tail variance.
- Session affinity behavior in production interacts with slot reclamation — the prototype used aggressive eviction after 90s idle; different TTLs will shift tradeoffs.
- Quantization (int8) reduces cost numbers but can widen p99 due to kernel path variance; more runs needed.

Open questions / discussion items
- Where to set the slab reservation size? We experimented with 1–4 token-slots per session. 2-slot gave best median/cost balance for target mix, but selection should be workload-tier driven.
- How to integrate with routing fallback? For p99 safety we need policy: if slab miss rate > X% during 1-min windows, fallback to prewarm for affected customers / routes. Value X needs tuning.
- Interaction with Dedicated capacity customers: some tenants prefer constant latency even at cost; treat as opt-out for slab reclamation.
- Telemetry: add metrics: slab_reserve_utilization, slab_eviction_rate, slab_fill_latency_histogram. We should plot these alongside p95/p99 in the console.

Practical next steps (short horizon)
- (Infra) Add slab-reservation counters + events (INFR-3789). Hook to the console traces so we can filter by route/model/tenant. (Owner: Miguel)
- (Benchmarking) Run heterogeneous-cluster sweep (A100+H100+T4) to measure variability envelope. (Owner: Jordan)
- (Product) Draft routing-fallback policy options for SLAed customers; propose default threshold and opt-out model. (Owner: Asha)
- (DX) Flesh out a one-page explainer for solutions-eng explaining when to pick slab vs prewarm. (Owner: Riley)

Quick notes for PM/infra sync
- If we roll slab with conservative defaults (2-slot per active session, 90s idle TTL, slab eviction LRU), we expect median unit-cost win ~25% for mid-tail web chat while limiting p99 regressions to within ~1.5x of prewarm in most windows.
- Recommend canary rollout to a small set of non-SLA tenants first (3–5 customers) and monitor slab_eviction_rate + p99 drift for 72h.

References & traces
- See INFR-3789 for the telemetry PR and raw logs.
- Perf harness: GH PR link above; benchmark scripts under /bench/slot-slab/ in the repo.
- Sketch confluence page (linked) contains plots exported from the runs (pngs) — this doc contains textual summaries in case images get stale.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Try TTL variants 30s/60s/120s and capture cost-delta curve; current 90s is naive.
- Add synthetic long-tail jitter to workload generator to stress p99.
- Check memory overhead per slab reservation: small but non-zero — track across model sizes (7B/13B/70B).

End of draft.

Action items appended in the console as quick tasks.
